# Hartree–Fock kinetic energy, continuum Coulomb Hamiltonian

Crisostomo, Levy and Burke, Can the Hartree–Fock kinetic energy exceed the exact kinetic energy? J. Chem. Phys. (2022), DOI 10.1063/5.0105684, arXiv:2206.11372, Eq. (7). This repository proposes an analytic counterexample for a finite radial confining local external potential, two electrons in R^3, Coulomb electron repulsion, and a symmetry-preserving singlet Hartree–Fock determinant.
Read continuum-witness.md for the Hamiltonian and estimates, independent-review.md for the mathematical audit, and VERIFICATION.md for exact Lean theorem coverage. The PDE and the identification of continuum minimizers with the bounds have a written derivation. The endpoint Lean theorem has explicit analytic hypotheses. A full Lean proof of the physical inequality reversal remains open in this repository.
The witness uses an artificial external field. The case of potentials generated solely by ordinary point nuclei remains a distinct question.
For the normalization bound with separate wavefunction and energy measures, see RayleighReweighting.normalized_energy in supplement/RayleighReweighting.lean. The constructor's second review in radial-audit.md checks the exterior boundary term and general complex spinors as well.

For the exact Lean statement, look up ContinuumHamiltonian.FixedRadialReversal in continuum/ContinuumHamiltonian.lean. Its target requires continuum exact and unrestricted spinor Hartree–Fock global minima, uniqueness of the HF ray, a radial closed shell, and strict kinetic reversal at the fixed physical field. The target is defined and remains unproved. Consult continuum/README.md before attributing a formal result.

For verified intermediate results search RadialProbe.spatial_margin (three-dimensional shell integral), HFKinetic.two_particle_remainder (finite-frequency squared-gradient estimate), GaussianCoulomb.second_moment (Gaussian radial integral equals 2/3), and HFExterior.weak_radial_maximum (weighted exterior comparison). These declaration names distinguish reusable results from the open physical endpoint.

Alternative analytic derivations of the removal-energy and density estimates appear in fourth-order-trial.md and squared-marginal-flux.md. Search for the quartic Gaussian double excitation, the Coulomb matrix of 1, P2, P4, and the Gaussian-transformed squared marginal with compact radial test functions. Two independent exact-arithmetic scripts accompany the trial.

For Section 5 search FixedRadialSectionFive.fixed_radial_stability and SectionFive.variational_stability_on_domain. For the Hilbert-space determinant geometry search SlaterGeometry.double_excitation_bound. For the radial tail search HFExterior.marginal_tail_of_weak_difference. Each result has hypotheses documented in continuum/README.md.
